purpose: Reproduce and measure the recovery time for the aicc_pg_restore.sh drill, which the SRV-07 design cited as ~5.4s without a run artifact.

environment.server_kind: standalone cluster (initdb + pg_ctl), scram-sha-256 auth, loopback only

dataset.description: Synthetic production-shaped dataset seeded through the aicc_app role after a full bootstrap + migrate provisioning pass (all 14 migrations applied, 55 relations incl. views).

procedure.timed_window: target database creation (CREATE DATABASE) through the post-restore information_schema.tables count -- the wait an operator experiences during a real recovery. Excludes argument parsing and checksum verification, which precede the timer.

result.variance: 0s across 4 consecutive runs at this dataset size, single restore job
result.conclusion: The restore step of the documented drill is real, reproducible, and completes in ~2s for a ~400k-row / 102MB live database on commodity hardware. This is a measurement at a specific, stated dataset size, not a universal constant -- RTO scales with data volume and pg_restore --jobs. It supersedes the previously unverified ~5.4s figure cited in the SRV-07 design, which had no run artifact behind it.

reproduction.seed_note: The seeding script used to generate this dataset is a one-off (not checked into the repository); reproduce with any generator that fills task/session/run/run_event via the aicc_app role, or substitute a real staging snapshot.
steps: read elapsed_seconds from the JSON written to --measure-out
